title: S12 auth-service — API surface
description: Port 7720, prefix AUT-. JWT (HS256) issue/verify/revoke + JWKS-style public key view. Endpoints: GET /healthz, /readyz, /keys, /stats; POST /token, /verify, /revoke. Tokens are compact JWTs signed with the in-crate HMAC-SHA256; the signing secret never leaves the service (only kid/alg/fingerprint are exposed). Revoke is idempotent by jti over a bounded set; key rotation retires the oldest active key but retained tokens keep verifying until evicted. Errors: AUT-2xx request/validation (400): 204 malformed token, 205 wrong alg, 206 unknown kid, 207 bad signature, 208 expired, 209 not-yet-valid, 210 revoked, 211 required scope missing, 212 semantic mismatch, 213/214 missing jti/token, 201/202/203 bad sub/scopes/ttl; AUT-0xx protocol/no-route (404/405).

tokenIssueRequest.description: POST /token — mint a token. 'sub' is required and non-empty; 'scopes' defaults to []; 'ttl_ns' is clamped to max_ttl_ns.

sub.description: Subject (identity) the token is issued for.

ttl_ns.description: Optional token lifetime; clamped to the configured max.

tokenIssueResponse.description: 200 — the issued token plus its metadata (IssuedToken.to_json). iat == nbf; exp == iat + effective ttl.

kid.description: Signing key id used; present in the token header.

tokenVerifyRequest.description: POST /verify — verify a token; optional 'scope' triggers a required-scope check (AUT-211 on failure).

scope.description: Optional required scope to assert on the token's scope list.

tokenVerifyResponse.description: 200 — FLAT claims object (no nested 'claims' wrapper) with kid and valid:true. On any verification failure the service answers the §1.2 error envelope with the specific AUT-2xx code and context.reason set to the VerifyFailure string.

aud.description: Present only when the token carried an audience.

tokenRevokeRequest.description: POST /revoke — revoke a jti; idempotent (re-revoking returns created:false and is not double-counted).

tokenRevokeResponse.description: 200 — revoked:true always; created distinguishes first-time from already-present.

keysListResponse.description: GET /keys — array of JWKS-style public views. The secret is NEVER present anywhere in the response; fingerprint is the first 16 hex chars of SHA-256 over the secret.

keyPublicView.description: SigningKey.public_view — the only form of a key ever exposed over HTTP.
